fix(custom-controls): forward extra link attributes, drop control options (#4662)

* fix(custom-controls): forward extra link attributes, drop control options

Custom control links handled kwargs inconsistently, and neither path was
right.

`ResourceComponent#render_link_to` (header and row bars) hand-picked the
kwargs it passed to `a_link`, so genuine HTML attributes never reached the
`<a>` — `link_to "Docs", url, rel: "noopener"` silently dropped the rel,
even though `ButtonComponent` already exposes a `prop :args, kind: :**`
wildcard for exactly this.

`ActionsComponent#render_item` (list dropdowns) did the opposite and
spread everything:

    link_to action.args[:path],
      class: action.args.delete(:class),
      **action.args.except(:path, :label, :icon)

Dropdown items render as plain links, not ButtonComponents, so the
styling options had nothing to land in and leaked into the markup as
`color="fuchsia"`. The internal plumbing `execute_block` merges in
(`as_index_control`, `item`) was one option name away from leaking too,
and `.delete(:class)` mutated the control's stored args, so a re-render
would drop the class.

Introduce `BaseControl::CONTROL_OPTIONS` — the keys a control consumes
itself — and have both paths exclude exactly those and forward the rest.
Extra attributes now reach the `<a>` in both contexts, while control
options and plumbing stay out of the HTML.

fix: stop Inter's contextual alternates rendering 0x0 as 0×0 in inputs (#4667)

Inter's calt OpenType feature substitutes a multiplication-sign glyph for
"x" between digits. Firefox applies full OpenType shaping inside form
controls, so typing 0x0 in any input visually becomes 0×0 (the value is
unaffected). Disable only contextual alternates on form fields, keeping
common ligatures intact.

Fix tab button scroll reset on lazy load; animate tab switching, add tab badges (#4664)

* Fix tab button scroll reset when turbo frames lazy load

When a tab button row has many tabs and becomes horizontally scrollable
(.tabs--scrollable with overflow-x-auto), clicking a lazy-loaded tab for
the first time causes the scroll position to snap back to the left.

Root cause: the tabs-overflow controller's update() method removes the
.tabs--scrollable class to measure whether buttons wrap. Removing
overflow-x-auto resets the browser's scrollLeft to 0. The method then
re-adds the class, but the scroll position is already gone. The
ResizeObserver fires when turbo-frame content loads and reflows the page.

Fix: capture scrollLeft at the start of update(), restore it after
re-applying the scrollable class. The entire operation runs synchronously
in one call, so no visual jump ever paints.

Fixes #4613

* Fix scroll capture: track on scroll event, not in update()

The previous fix captured scrollLeft inside update(), but by then the
browser had already reset it during page reflow. Now we track scroll
position via a scroll event listener so we always have the last known
position ready to restore after the class toggle.

* Sync tab button scroll position across panel copies

The previous fixes preserved scrollLeft on a single tabs row, but each
tab panel renders its own copy of the buttons row — clicking a tab hides
one panel and reveals a sibling whose row was never scrolled, so the
buttons still snapped back to the start.

Store the scroll position on the shared .tab-group container whenever a
row is scrolled, and restore from it whenever any row is (re)measured.
The revealed panel's row picks up the exact position of the row the user
just scrolled, so the button list stays visually still across tab
switches and lazy frame loads.

Fixes #4613

* Morph active tab indicator between tabs via view transitions

Extract the active tab's underline from a border on the wrapper into a
dedicated .tabs__indicator element, and wrap the panel swap in
document.startViewTransition(). Naming only the indicator element means
just the accent bar glides from the old tab to the new one — labels swap
instantly instead of stretching. The name is applied only for the
duration of the transition, so multiple tab groups never collide, and
the root crossfade is suppressed via a scoped marker class so the rest
of the page doesn't flash. Browsers without the API just switch
instantly, as before.

Also clip vertical overflow on the scrollable row: overflow-x: auto
computes overflow-y to auto, and the indicator's 1px overlap of the
container border created a spurious 1px vertical scrollbar.

* Animate tab group height when switching to a different-size panel

Name the .tab-group container during the tab-switch view transition so
its box animates to the new panel's height and the old content
crossfades into the new, instead of snapping. Snapshots keep their
natural height; the image pair clips the taller one while the box
resizes. The indicator stays its own named capture, so it still morphs
independently of the group snapshot.

* Hold tab group height while lazy content loads

Switching to a not-yet-loaded tab resized the group twice — down to the
small loading placeholder, then up to the real content — bouncing the
page and triggering scroll anchoring jumps.

Now the group is frozen at its current size (height + overflow clip)
when the incoming panel has a pending turbo frame, and released with a
single animated resize when the frame finishes loading. Switching away
mid-load or disconnecting releases the hold immediately so no stale
inline styles stick around (or end up in Turbo's page cache).

The view transition boilerplate is extracted into animate() so the tab
swap and the hold release share the same naming/cleanup path.

* Support a badge option on resource tabs

Wires the existing Avo::UI::Tabs::TabComponent badge prop through the tab DSL. Pass a renderable (e.g. Avo::UI::CountComponent) via tab badge: to show a count pill next to the tab label.

* Release the tab group height hold on frame load failures

turbo:frame-load covers success and Avo's /failed_to_load fallback for
500s, but a response missing the frame (turbo:frame-missing) or a
network error (turbo:fetch-request-error) fired neither, leaving the
group frozen at the held height until the next tab switch. Release on
those too.

* Skip tab view transitions under prefers-reduced-motion

The panel swap ran inside the startViewTransition callback, whose timing
is unreliable in headless Chrome — CI clicked a tab and the panel never
switched. Reduced motion now takes the synchronous swap path, and the
Cuprite driver forces --force-prefers-reduced-motion so system tests are
deterministic.

Also updates the tablist assertions for the badge demo on the user
resource (group_3 was cancelled in CI before it could catch them) and
fixes eslint offenses in the controller.

* Add resize_sidebar translations for all locales

Main added avo.resize_sidebar / avo.resize_sidebar_hint to the en locale
only (resizable sidebar), so the i18n missing-keys check fails on every
PR's merge ref. Translate the two keys into the other 18 locales.

* Force a fine pointer / hover-capable device in system tests

GitHub's Linux runners have no pointing device, so headless Chrome
reports `pointer: none` / `hover: none` and CSS gated on a precise
pointer — like the sidebar resize handle's R8 media query — collapses to
display: none, failing all 17 sidebar_resize_spec examples on the merge
ref (and on main itself). Blink settings pin the device capabilities to
mouse-like everywhere so these specs behave the same on macOS and CI.

AVO-1445: Resolve field help/placeholder/include_blank from translation_key siblings (#4652)

* feat(fields): resolve help/placeholder/include_blank from translation_key siblings

Fields resolve `#{translation_key}.help`, `.placeholder`, and
`.include_blank` when no explicit option is passed, so admin code no
longer needs English literals or verbose I18n.t calls. Explicit options
still take precedence.

Refactors the built-in placeholder defaults on select/country/belongs_to/
has_one into a `default_placeholder` override so sibling translations can
apply before the built-in fallback.

Fixes AVO-1445

* fix(fields): route frame field placeholder through translation siblings

FrameBaseField overrode #placeholder entirely, so has_one/has_many/array
fields never consulted translated_option(:placeholder) or default_placeholder.
Replace the override with a default_placeholder so BaseField#placeholder's
shared flow (sibling translation -> default -> ExecutionContext) applies,
and drop the now-redundant HasOneField#default_placeholder.

Add ejectable `avo-overrides.css` and `avo-overrides.js`

Ship two empty, ejectable files Avo auto-loads on every screen: avo-overrides.css (after avo/application.css) and avo-overrides.js (after avo/application.js, so window.Stimulus is available). Eject via `rails g avo:eject --partial :avo_overrides_css | :avo_overrides_js | :asset_overrides`. No-build escape hatch for CSS-variable theming and small Stimulus/Turbo snippets.

fix(ui): wire up card body padding via .card--padded modifier (#4650)

The CardComponent's padding prop was effectively dead — the template never
bound a padding class, so passing it did nothing.

Add a padded prop (matching the CSS modifier) wired to .card--padded (p-4 on
.card__body), defaulting to false so cards holding wide content (index tables,
scrollers) stay flush to the edge. Opt in for free-form content:

  panel.with_card(padded: true)   # or ui.card(padded: true)

Also drop the block of commented-out scaffolding methods from the component.

fix(hotkeys): ignore hotkeys on stale detached elements (#4647)

When a Turbo body replacement leaves Avo (e.g. clicking a broken resource
renders Rails' error page), @github/hotkey keeps its references to the old
sidebar links. Pressing a hotkey like "p" then fired hotkey-fire on the
detached link and, since it was no longer in the DOM, hotkeyFireHandler
early-returned without preventDefault, so @github/hotkey ran its default
action and .click()ed the stale link, navigating away.

Guard hotkeyFireHandler on el.isConnected so hotkeys are inert on non-Avo
pages, letting you type freely (e.g. in web-console) on the error screen.

Fix NoMethodError on Avo::CoursesController#cities by defining CoursePolicy#cities?

The custom cities action (country→cities dropdown JSON endpoint) routes
through Avo's authorize_action, which calls cities? on CoursePolicy. With
explicit_authorization, the missing method raised NoMethodError in Pundit.

Make nested Course links work by defining association policy methods

The links has_many (nested form via avo-nested) never appeared on the Course
new/edit form. Under explicit_authorization, Avo denies an association field
when its per-association policy method is missing.

Two policies are consulted because the field is authorized against its
field_resource:
- show view: not nested -> field_resource is Course -> CoursePolicy#view_links?
- new/edit:  nested     -> field_resource is the CourseLink resource ->
  Course::LinkPolicy#view_links?

Add the permissive *_links? set to BOTH CoursePolicy (show + saving) and
Course::LinkPolicy (nested form render), mirroring TeamPolicy's *_memberships?.
Verified end to end: nested add + save persists a Course::Link.

Fix solid_cable: isolate cable DB migrations from the primary

The cable SQLite database had no migrations_paths, so it defaulted to
db/migrate and ran ALL primary migrations against SQLite on deploy
(db:prepare) — blowing up on `array: true` (CreateSolidCableMessages never
ran; the app looked like it was migrating the whole schema into SQLite).

Scope the cable DB to its own db/cable_migrate path with a single
create_solid_cable_messages migration. Now db:prepare migrates Postgres
(primary) and the SQLite cable DB independently; the cable DB only ever gets
solid_cable_messages.

Run solid_cable on a dedicated SQLite database

Action Cable pub/sub moves off Redis to solid_cable, backed by its own
SQLite database (storage/cable_<env>.sqlite3) via a multi-database config.
The primary app database stays on Postgres.

- Gemfile: add sqlite3
- database.yml: primary (Postgres) + cable (SQLite) per env
- cable.yml: solid_cable adapter with connects_to cable in dev/prod
- db/cable_schema.rb: solid_cable_messages schema for the cable DB

Note: SQLite cable DB is single-machine only; multiple web instances would
not share broadcasts. Deploy release step must create/load the cable DB.

Show collaboration timeline by defining its policy methods

avo-collaboration gates the timeline on collaboration_view_timeline? /
_create_entry? / _destroy_entry?. With explicit_authorization, a missing
policy method is denied, so the timeline never rendered. Add permissive
defaults to BaseAvoPolicy so every collaboration-enabled resource shows it.
